A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AHCPTQ for SAM. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained Appendices A–D against v2's additional Appendices E–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO segmentation experiments, ablations, FPGA measurements, and ImageNet classification results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds initialization-search sensitivity, weight-grouping experiments, and qualitative segmentation comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix F introduces an optional adaptation applying CAG with 32 groups to model weights, replacing per-channel weight quantization in that experiment. The main HLUQ quantizer, activation-grouping algorithm, reconstruction objective, and hardware procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover COCO instance segmentation with four detector-based prompt sources and ImageNet classification with DeiT. The new appendix studies remain within SAM/YOLOX segmentation and introduce no distinct dataset, task, or input environment.

E2.justification: The segmentation, ImageNet, and hardware comparator sets are unchanged. Figure 15 uses the existing floating-point, BRECQ, QDrop, and PTQ4SAM comparisons; newly cited RPTQ is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds an expanded initialization search over alpha from 0.1 to 0.9 and beta from 1/8 to 7/8; Appendix F tests 32 weight groups. Existing calibration and evaluation settings remain unchanged. New settings have labeling ambiguities: Tables 5–6 say W5A6, whereas Appendix E says W5A5; Figure 15 says SAM-B, whereas Appendix G says SAM-H.

E4.justification: Appendices E–G add focused checks of initialization-search sensitivity, CAG's applicability to weight quantization, and segmentation-mask quality across four visual examples. Existing component, quantizer, activation-group-count, and channel-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices do not change. The existing 100-sample channel-similarity analysis is retained, and the new experiments add no seed information, run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. New Tables 5–6 report extended-search scores of 13.1/32.0/35.3 and weight-grouping scores of 12.3/30.8/34.3, alongside default scores of 13.4/31.8/35.4. These are additional experimental conditions, not revisions to the original scores. Figure 15 adds qualitative mask results.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, reconstruction loss, HLUQ equations, and calibration objective in Equations 1–8 remain unchanged. The appended experiments introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: HLUQ and CAG enable accurate low-bit SAM quantization with hardware compatibility. The headline 36.6% mAP, 7.89× speedup, and 8.64× energy-efficiency claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the expanded-search results as supporting a small initialization grid, the weight experiment as showing CAG generalizability, and the visual examples as demonstrating boundary preservation and practical robustness. The existing limitation concerning future CPU/GPU deployment remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promise of code availability upon acceptance with a stated code release and repository address. It also specifies the extended search grid and 32-group weight configuration. Existing implementation and FPGA details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds RPTQ and Xia et al.'s universal powers-of-two accelerator, distinguishing progressive CAG from static grouping and emphasizing retraining demands of nonuniform quantizers. Its duplicated Additive Powers-of-Two reference represents an already cited work, not another distinct addition.

P1.justification: Limited edits clarify motivation and grouping, streamline Section 3.4, remove some appendix pointers, and correct AHCPT to AHCPTQ. v2 also adds an author, acknowledgments, and Appendices E–G. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two small tables and the four-example, five-column segmentation comparison in Figure 15. It relocates Algorithm 1, Figure 4, Table 1, and other retained displays as text reflows; existing figures and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix E provides evidence supporting the small initialization grid, while Appendices F–G document weight-grouping behavior and segmentation appearance. Together with code-access information, these modestly strengthen validation and reproducibility documentation. Conflicting bit-width labels in Tables 5–6 and model names around Figure 15 reduce the additions' clarity, limiting the overall gain.
